title: When "Except Bone Transform" is enabled in Retarget Import, the bone tracks get erased.
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.2.stable.steam [ed1daf0bf], v4.8.dev.custom_build [ca871ccc9]

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1088) - AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 47.01 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

According to the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/retargeting_3d_skeletons.html#except-bone-transform), this option is supposed to leave the bone tracks, but in practice it also erases the bone tracks. Therefore, the character does not move.

The `Walking_A` clip in the attached MRP contains 21 bone tracks. Regardless of the option, there should be 21 remaining, but if the option is enabled, the count drops to zero.

This error also occurs during import (44 times in both 4.7.2 and master).
```
ERROR: Index (uint32_t)p_track = 30 is out of bounds (tracks.size() = 30).
ERROR: Index (uint32_t)p_track = 15 is out of bounds (tracks.size() = 15).
```

The cause has been identified, and I plan to post a PR soon.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Extract the MRP and double-click `character.glb` to open the Advanced Import window, then select `Skeleton3D`. `BoneMap` (`SkeletonProfileHumanoid`) is set, and `Except Bone Transform` is turned on.
2. When you run `main.tscn`, you can see that the animation does not play and the character is standing in a T-pose.
3. Turn off the option and click `Reimport`; the number of tracks will return to 21, and the animation works properly.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[except-bone-transform.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32591777/except-bone-transform.zip)

The 3D assets and animations are from KayKit Character Animations 1.1 (CC0).
